newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia says not guaranteeing Bakun project.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia says not guaranteeing Bakun project.

text.p: The Malaysian government is providing a "letter of comfort" to banks involved in financing the $5.5 billion Bakun dam, but has not given a financial guarantee to the project, Leo Moggie, minister of energy, telecommunications and posts said on Thursday.

"The Malaysian government has always been supportive of the Bakun dam project. It is considered a national project. We have agreed to provide a letter of comfort to the banks involved in the bridging finance to the contractors pending the (Bakun stock) listing," Moggie said.
But, he added, "It is not a guarantee. The Malaysian government is not in the habit of providing guarantees to the private sector."
"After the stock exchange listing, the letter of comfort then lapses," Moggie added. He was speaking to reporters at a signing ceremony between Bakun Hydro-Electric Corp (BHEC) and its shareholders.

The Bakun dam, being constructed in the rainforests of Sarawak state on Borneo island, is expected to be completed by 2003. The stock listing of BHEC, the holding company for the dam, is expected to be done in June this year.
Ting Pek Khiing, executive chairman of Ekran Bhd, which is the main contractor of the project, confirmed that 10 percent of BHEC would be offered to foreign and local institutional investors.
Previously, Ekran had said 10 percent of BHEC would be offered to foreigners. Talk emerged last week that the portion for foreign investors would be scrapped because of lukewarm response.
But the adviser for the initial public offering (IPO) denied such speculation last week.
Questioned by reporters on Thursday, Ting said the 10 percent was also opened up to Malaysian institutions because of interest from that segment.
But he said that the shares would be on a "first come first served basis". He did not elaborate.
On Thursday, the Financial Times quoted one of Bakun's lead contractors ABB Asea Brown Boveri as saying that Malaysia had agreed to guarantee financing of the project.
The newspaper quoted ABB's chief executive Goran Lindahl, who spoke on Wednesday after meetings with Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad and his Cabinet.
Mahathir has been the biggest supporter of the project, which drew fire from environmentalists and tribal people displaced by the dam.
The dam will create a reservoir the size of Singapore and clear 69,000 hectares of forest land.
The stock listing will be the single largest on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange, floating 1.5 billion shares of 2.00 ringgit each in an exercise to raise 3.0 billion ringgit.
Ekran is the largest shareholder of Bakun, with a 32 percent stake. Other major shareholders are the Sarawak State government and the Sarawak Electricity Supply Corp.
Malaysia's national pension fund the Employees' Provident Fund, electric utility Tenaga Nasional Bhd and the Malaysian public will also be shareholders of BHEC.
